builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: AutoRAGBench: A Benchmark for LLM Agents Automating RAG System Development
summary: The approach replaces manual, iterative RAG pipeline engineering (chunking, retrieval, prompting, and reranking design) with an autonomous LLM coding agent that builds and refines the system in an open code space. Costs are frontier-model API spend over multi-hour agent runs, plus sandboxed execution infrastructure and task-specific evaluation harnesses to give the agent reliable feedback. It can fail when the reader lacks an automated scoring signal for the agent to iterate against, when the agent overfits to that metric, or when weaker models than the benchmarked frontier configurations produce systems below the human baseline.
rationale: The reader ships RAG systems and can plausibly offload iterative RAG pipeline tuning to a frontier coding agent via API, but the reported gains come from a single six-hour, nine-task benchmark with top-tier models, so workload-specific validation is required before relying on it.

claims.statement: The approach replaces manual, iterative RAG pipeline engineering (chunking, retrieval, prompting, and reranking design) with an autonomous LLM coding agent that builds and refines the system in an open code space. Costs are frontier-model API spend over multi-hour agent runs, plus sandboxed execution infrastructure and task-specific evaluation harnesses to give the agent reliable feedback. It can fail when the reader lacks an automated scoring signal for the agent to iterate against, when the agent overfits to that metric, or when weaker models than the benchmarked frontier configurations produce systems below the human baseline.

GPT-6.1 Sol with Codex CLI achieves an average score of 56.1 across nine RAG development tasks versus a composite human-SOTA baseline of 44.4, and improves human-designed starting systems by 16.6 points on average across seven tasks.
